# ViewMagnet — Full content index for AI crawlers

> Predict, create, and publish YouTube videos in one app. ML-driven analyzer
> (74.58% balanced accuracy on a held-out test set), script writer with four
> proven viral frameworks, full studio editor, and a one-click distribution hub.

This is the long-form companion to [/llms.txt](https://viewmagnet.io/llms.txt).
It restates the most citation-worthy content on the site in plain text so an
AI crawler can ingest the substance without rendering JavaScript. Source of
truth for any disagreement is the live page.

---

# Methodology

## How ViewMagnet predicts virality

ViewMagnet runs four ML models, each specialised for a different stage of a
video's lifecycle:

1. **Pre-upload (XGBoost gradient boosted trees)** — 74.58% balanced accuracy
   on an internal held-out test set. Predicts whether an idea + title +
   thumbnail will beat the channel's trailing-90-day median for the same
   length bucket (Shorts vs long-form). Used in the Video Analyzer.

2. **Early growth (Day 1 → target)** — ≈82–86% directional accuracy.
   Extrapolates expected 30-day view count from the first 24 hours.

3. **Velocity (Day 7 → Day 30)** — XGBoost regression, ≈90% within 1 std dev
   of true Day-30 view count.

4. **Mature (Day 14 → Day 30)** — XGBoost regression, ≈94% within 1 std dev.
   Final-fit projection used in the Velocity Tracker once early-life noise
   has decayed.

All four accuracy numbers are **internal benchmarks** on our own data, not
externally validated.

## What "balanced accuracy" means

Most uploads (~70%) underperform their channel's trailing median. A naive
model that always predicts "underperform" would score ~70% raw accuracy
while being completely useless — it could never flag a winner. Balanced
accuracy averages the recall on each class (overperformer vs underperformer),
so a useful model has to be right on both. 74.58% balanced accuracy means:

- ~75% of true overperformers are correctly flagged as likely winners.
- ~75% of true underperformers are correctly flagged as likely
  underperformers.
- No free lunch from the majority class.

It is **not** a guarantee that 74.58% of "likely viral" predictions actually
go viral. Virality has a heavy luck tail; the model is right about relative
ranking, not absolute view counts.

## Training data

- Hundreds of thousands of public YouTube videos across every major category
  (educational, gaming, lifestyle, business, music, comedy, reviews, news
  commentary).
- Both Shorts and long-form, kept in separate length buckets.
- Full thumbnail images + titles + descriptions + tags + auto-captioned
  transcripts.
- Channel context: subscriber count, trailing-90-day median, upload cadence,
  hit rate.

**Deliberately excluded**: private analytics (CTR, average view duration,
retention curves), data from the creator's own channel without opt-in, and
any personally identifiable information. The pre-upload model only ever sees
what a third-party tool would have at upload time, so the score is honest
about what's actually predictable from the public surface.

## Predictions → recommendations

A single number is a verdict, not a tool. The recommendation engine:

1. Explains the prediction with **SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)** —
   the same library used in research papers, attributing a fraction of the
   predicted score to each input feature.
2. Rolls features up into three buckets matching how the YouTube algorithm
   actually evaluates a video: **START** (did people click?), **KEEP** (did
   they stay watching?), **REPEAT** (did they want to come back?).
3. Routes the lowest-scoring bucket to the right tool: Hook Lab for Start,
   Script Writer for Keep / Repeat, A/B Tester to validate the change.

## Academic citations behind the methodology

- Chen &amp; Guestrin (2016). XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System. KDD '16.
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.02754
- Lundberg &amp; Lee (2017). A Unified Approach to Interpreting Model
  Predictions. NeurIPS. https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.07874
- Brodersen et al. (2010). The Balanced Accuracy and Its Posterior
  Distribution. ICPR. https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/5597285
- He &amp; Garcia (2009). Learning from Imbalanced Data. IEEE TKDE.
  https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/5128907
- Provost &amp; Fawcett (2013). Data Science for Business (ch. 7–8). O'Reilly.

# Analyzer Guide — Start / Keep / Repeat

Every video on every platform competes on the same three questions, and
ViewMagnet scores each one separately:

- **START**: Did people click to watch? (CTR; title + thumbnail packaging.)
- **KEEP**: Did they stay watching? (AVD; hook + pacing + structure.)
- **REPEAT**: Did they want to come back? (Saves, shares, return visits.)

The lowest score is the **bottleneck** — the highest-leverage thing to fix.

## Start bottleneck

**Diagnosis**: title and thumbnail aren't earning enough clicks. Even great
content can't reach without the packaging working first.

**Symptoms**:
- CTR below the channel's typical baseline.
- Strong retention on the few who do click (content is fine, packaging isn't).
- Thumbnail is "competent" but blends in.
- Title summarizes the video instead of opening a curiosity gap.

**Fix**: rewrite the hook to open a gap, make the thumbnail readable at 2cm,
validate with the A/B Tester. Sample rewrites:

- Weak: "Here are 3 tips to grow your Instagram"
- Strong: "Stop posting Reels until you've fixed the mistake 87% of new
  accounts make in their first week"
- Why: converts a generic tip list into a mistake callout — viewer can't
  tell if they're making the mistake without watching.

## Keep bottleneck

**Diagnosis**: viewers click but drop off early. Pacing, structure, or a
hook that over-promises.

**Symptoms**:
- CTR healthy, Average View Duration well below typical for the length
  bucket.
- Sharp drop-off in the first 15–30s (creator-side folk wisdom, not
  peer-reviewed).
- Long monologues without re-anchoring curiosity.
- Hook promises something the video buries 4 minutes in.

**Fix**: tighten the hook → payoff loop. Use Progressive Debunking to keep
viewers expecting the next revelation. Cut dead air. Re-anchor curiosity
every 15–30s.

## Repeat bottleneck

**Diagnosis**: viewers watch once but don't save, share, or come back.

**Symptoms**:
- Low saves/shares relative to view count.
- Return-viewer rate trending down.
- Generic comments ("nice video!").
- No named, repeatable structure.

**Fix**: add named systems (give your method a name viewers can search),
build in clear lead-magnet payoffs. Use Lead Magnet or Authority Myth-Buster
frameworks — both engineer saves and shares.

## Balanced (no clear bottleneck)

When Start, Keep, and Repeat are all within ~8 points of each other the
Analyzer labels the video "balanced". That doesn't mean great — it means
there isn't a single weak link. Strategy: pick the lowest of the three and
lift it by 5–10 points; once one becomes a clear leader, attack the new
lowest. Balanced videos in the 40–60 band usually need a structural rebuild
rather than a tactical fix.

## Academic citations behind the rewrite patterns

- Loewenstein (1994). The Psychology of Curiosity. *Psychological Bulletin*.
  https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.116.1.75
- Berger &amp; Milkman (2012). What Makes Online Content Viral? *JMR*.
  https://doi.org/10.1509/jmr.10.0353
- Kahneman &amp; Tversky (1979). Prospect Theory. *Econometrica*.
  https://doi.org/10.2307/1914185
- Schindler &amp; Yalch (2006). Sharp vs round numbers in advertising claims.
  *Advances in Consumer Research*, Vol. 33.
- Berger (2013). *Contagious: Why Things Catch On* (ch. 4 — Practical Value).
  https://jonahberger.com/books/contagious/

# The 4 Viral Script Frameworks

Every script ViewMagnet generates is built on one of four frameworks. The
taxonomy is adapted from creator **Chris Girbu** (https://www.chrisgirbu.com/).

## 1. Authority Myth-Buster (primary goal: trust)

Build trust fast with new audiences by opening with a contrarian hook that
challenges conventional wisdom, anchoring authority, then delivering the
real answer in three parts.

Structure:
1. Contrarian Hook (8s)
2. Authority Anchor (10s)
3. Solution Part 1 (30s)
4. Solution Part 2 (30s)
5. Solution Part 3 (30s)
6. Ideological CTA (15s)

## 2. Delta Shift (primary goal: saves)

The highest save-rate format we measure (internal benchmark). Shows the gap
between baseline behavior and what the top 1% actually do.

Structure:
1. Baseline (15s)
2. Delta (the top-1% move) (25s)
3. Single Takeaway (15s)
4. Save CTA (5s)

## 3. Progressive Debunking / Iceberg (primary goal: retention)

Maximises watch time by structuring the video as a sequence of revelations,
each deeper than the last. The viewer keeps watching specifically to hear
what's underneath.

Structure:
1. Polarizing Topic (10s)
2. Dismiss the Surface (25s)
3. Reveal Layer 1 (25s)
4. Reveal Layer 2 (25s)
5. Final Revelation (25s)
6. Loop Back (5s)

## 4. Lead Magnet (primary goal: leads)

Fills auto-DM funnels with keyword CTAs. Promises a named system, teases a
blurred asset, breaks the system into rapid steps, ends with a keyword CTA
("comment X and I'll DM you the template").

Note: the internal slug for this framework is `hype_heit` (legacy name from
an earlier creator we credit). The user-facing display name is "Lead Magnet
Framework". Renamed because the legacy label wasn't an expanded acronym and
read as branded jargon — see the framework page for context.

Structure:
1. Named System Promise (8s)
2. Blurred Asset Tease (10s)
3. Rapid Breakdown 1 (15s)
4. Rapid Breakdown 2 (15s)
5. Rapid Breakdown 3 (15s)
6. Keyword CTA (7s)

## The 6 hook types (Hook Lab taxonomy)

Hook Lab scores every hook against six types. One is weak (the anti-pattern),
five are strong. Taxonomy overlaps with Brendan Kane's *Hook Point*
(https://hookpoint.com/).

- **Summary** (weak): restates what the video will be about.
- **Mistake Callout**: identifies an error the viewer might be making.
- **Belief Destruction**: directly challenges a belief the viewer holds.
- **Authority Anchor**: establishes credibility before the value lands.
- **Stake Reversal**: reframes what the viewer thinks they should be doing
  as the actual problem. Leans on loss aversion (Kahneman &amp; Tversky 1979).
- **Specificity**: uses precise numbers ("cut 5 things, 90 minutes total")
  rather than vague claims ("save lots of time"). Backed by Schindler &amp;
  Yalch 2006.

## Which framework should I pick?

- **Building a new audience / contrarian niche** → Authority Myth-Buster
- **Maximising saves / shares** → Delta Shift
- **Holding viewers for 10+ minute videos** → Progressive Debunking
- **Building an email or DM list** → Lead Magnet

# Honest disclosures

These are flagged on the live pages and we'd appreciate the same when
citing the content:

- **74.58% balanced accuracy** is a ViewMagnet-internal benchmark on our
  held-out test set. Not externally validated.
- **The "~70/30 over/underperform split"** is our dataset observation, not
  a peer-reviewed claim.
- **"Delta Shift has the highest save rate format we measure"** is an
  internal benchmark only.
- **Specific retention numbers** (drop-off at 15–30s, first 10s curve
  inflection) are creator-economy folk wisdom, not peer-reviewed papers.
- **The four-framework taxonomy** is adapted from Chris Girbu, not original
  to ViewMagnet.
- **The six hook-type taxonomy** overlaps with Brendan Kane's *Hook Point*.

# AI Integrations — ViewMagnet MCP server (`viewmagnet-mcp`)

ViewMagnet ships a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
server that lets any MCP-compatible AI agent (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline)
call the ViewMagnet toolkit on a user's behalf. The package is published as
[`viewmagnet-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/viewmagnet-mcp).

## Install

```
npx viewmagnet-mcp install
```

The installer detects Claude Desktop, Cursor, and Cline if they're installed,
prompts for a Personal Access Token (generated at
https://viewmagnet.io/dashboard/api-tokens), and writes the MCP server entry
into the matching config file(s). Existing MCP server entries in the user's
config are preserved.

For a manual install or unsupported clients, `npx viewmagnet-mcp install --print`
prints the JSON snippet to stdout without touching disk.

## Auth model

The MCP server authenticates to the ViewMagnet API using a **Personal Access
Token (PAT)** — never the user's password and never a long-lived JWT. Token
format: `vm_pat_<8-hex-prefix>_<32-hex-secret>`. The backend stores only the
indexed prefix and a sha256 of the secret half; a database leak cannot be
replayed.

Tokens are revocable from the dashboard, may be scoped (`read`, `write`,
`admin` — v1 records scopes for grandfathering; v2 enforces them
per-endpoint), and may optionally hard-expire (30/90/365 days or never).

## Tools (v1 — 10 sync tools)

| Tool | Backend call | Use when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewmagnet_analyze_video` | `POST /analyze` | Predict score/tier/bottleneck for a YouTube URL. |
| `viewmagnet_list_frameworks` | `GET /scripts/frameworks` | Discover the 4 script frameworks. |
| `viewmagnet_generate_script` | `POST /scripts/generate-framework` | Generate a full framework-based script. |
| `viewmagnet_score_hook` | `POST /hooks/score` | Score a hook on belief challenge / urgency / specificity. |
| `viewmagnet_list_hook_types` | `GET /hooks/types` | Discover the 6 hook archetypes. |
| `viewmagnet_detect_highlights` | `POST /shorts/detect-highlights` | Find clip-worthy moments in a long video. |
| `viewmagnet_analyze_pacing` | `POST /pacing/analyze` | Pacing grade + cut recommendations. |
| `viewmagnet_score_title` | `POST /titles/score` | CTR-focused title scoring. |
| `viewmagnet_generate_titles` | `POST /titles/generate` | Generate title variations. |
| `viewmagnet_get_outcomes` | `GET /distribution/outcomes` | Pull published-video performance + recommendation attribution. |

Deferred to v2 (need backend job-polling refactors): clip extraction, Studio
render, scheduled publish.

## Example prompts (so the agent picks the right tools)

- "Analyze https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ and tell me what to fix."
- "Write a Lead Magnet script about morning routines."
- "Score this hook: 'Most diets are designed to fail.'"
- "Find the 5 best clip moments in https://youtu.be/..."
- "Which framework actually performed best for my last 30 videos?"

## Config

| Setting | Env var | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API base URL | `VM_API_URL` | `https://api.viewmagnet.com` |
| PAT | `VM_PAT_TOKEN` | _(required)_ |
| Request timeout (ms) | `VM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `60000` |
| Verbose stderr logs | `VM_MCP_VERBOSE` | `0` |

The MCP server runs over stdio and is spawned by the host agent — no port,
no daemon, no inbound networking.

---

# Public REST API documentation

The complete REST API surface (130+ endpoints) is published as an
OpenAPI 3.1 document at:

- Spec (JSON): https://api.viewmagnet.com/openapi.json
- Interactive reference (Scalar): https://viewmagnet.io/docs

The reference page groups endpoints by user-journey tags
(Authentication → API Tokens → analyze → scripts → hooks → studio
→ distribution → admin) and supports "Try it" requests directly
against production using a Personal Access Token.

Two named bearer schemes are exposed in the spec's
`components.securitySchemes`:

| Scheme | Format | Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PersonalAccessToken` | `vm_pat_<prefix>_<secret>` | Scripts, MCP server, CI, third-party agents |
| `SessionJWT`          | opaque JWT                  | First-party browser sessions only |

All errors return the envelope `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "details"}}`. Rate limits are tier-based and surface as `429` with a `Retry-After` header.
